messages:
matt: Heads-up: seeing long-tail gRPC stalls for pod->pod streaming on GPU jobs in eu-west-1 since the CNI ipip rollout last night. A few pods hit 30-60s stalls then catch up. No obvious CPU/GPU pressure.
alex: How widespread? single nodepair or multiple AZs?
matt: Multiple nodepairs across two k8s nodes, different AZs. All affected flows are heavy token streams (long-lived bidi gRPC). Short RPCs fine.
alex: Can you paste a small tcpdump snippet from a repro pod+node? suspect fragmentation/DF interactions.
matt: sure, i grabbed a snippet from node1->node2 when a stream stalled:

```
22:14:02.123456 IP 10.32.5.12 > 10.48.7.9: UDP, length 1420
22:14:02.123789 IP 10.32.5.12 > 10.48.7.9: Frag 1432: offset 0, flags +more
22:14:02.124001 IP 10.32.5.12 > 10.48.7.9: Frag 1432: offset 180, flags 0
```

looks like ipip encapsulation added ~20 bytes and packets are being fragmented mid-path.

natalie: path includes cloud peering + nat gateway for egress between AZs — we have a clamp on the transit router: MTU got reduced to 1420 recently due to a routing appliance rule. ipip adds ~20 so end-to-end drops below DF threshold.

oncall-bot: ALERT: grpc-stream-tail-latency spike (eu-west-1) — 47 instances above 10s in last 5m

jen: Are we using RDMA for these GPU nodes? fragmentation kills RDMA, but we usually don't cross-host RDMA for these jobs.
matt: RDMA not in play for these streams (TCP gRPC). Problem is repeated fragment reassembly + gRPC flow-control: long streaming responses rely on continuous small frames; when fragmentation/clobbering happens, the TCP retrans/tail leads to large stalls. Also observed lower application-level throughput when GSO/GRO isn't working across encapsulation.

alex: quick checks: net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing on nodes? MSS clamp on iptables? CNI MTU config?
matt: tcp_mtu_probing=0 currently. CNI ipip default mtu = 1440, node interface mtus 1500, but transit clamp 1420 makes ipip payload > path mtu.

natalie: root cause seems to be combination: ipip encap + transit MTU clamp => path MTU < inner payload => fragmentation. Some routers are dropping fragments or reassembling poorly which breaks streaming.

jen: Temporary mitigations:
- flip CNI to use GENEVE/encap that preserves GSO/GRO (if our kernel offloads work better)
- reduce pod MTU to 1350 via CNI config (fast but needs rolling daemonset restart)
- enable net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on nodes and restart pods
- add an egress MSS clamp rule on the NAT/router side

alex: MSS-clamp iptables example we used before:
```
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
That buys time without changing CNI.

matt: i tested clamp locally and gRPC tail latency dropped from 28s -> <300ms on a repro stream. Good short-term.

natalie: Long-term we should avoid IPIP for cross-AZ heavy streaming, prefer geneve/vxlan with offload and enable GSO/GRO for encap. Also file a cloud ticket to lift the MTU clamp or move transit appliances out of the datapath.

sre-bot: ACTIONS: @natalie open ticket to cloud infra (MTU clamp uplift). @alex prepare MSS-clamp DaemonSet. @matt run canary (CNI podMTU change) in eu-west-1-small pool.

jen: +1. prioritize MSS-clamp DS as hotfix, then plan geneve test in staging.

matt: I'll push the MSS-clamp DS now, run canary and share perf dashboards. If anyone sees any other affected services ping here.

alex: ping when DS is live, i'll watch packet drops/fragment counters on nodes.

jen: thanks team. :thumbsup:
